findings_qualitative.value: HDO and CH3CHO are more compact than C17O along the equatorial plane

evidence.quote: HDO and CH$_3$CHO are more compact than C$^{17}$O, which is more elongated along the equatorial plane.

claims.hypothesis: HDO and CH3CHO trace chemically enriched gas at the centrifugal barrier of the HH 212 disc
claims.experiment: Cycle 4 imaging, PV diagrams and centroid fits
claims.result: Linear PV gradient, emission radius ~60 au
claims.finding: Emission arises from an edge-on ring where envelope meets disc, probably through low-velocity accretion shocks

evidence.quote: This is most likely the signature of emission from an edge-on ring of chemically enriched warm gas.

claims.hypothesis: Physical conditions of HDO and CH3CHO gas

evidence.quote: the LVG analysis of the HDO emission at 335 K severely constrains the volume density, n$_{\rm H_2}$ $\geq$ 10$^8$ cm$^{-3}$

claims.hypothesis: iCOMs and HDO are outflowing in a disc wind
claims.result: Peaks offset from equatorial plane at ±1 km/s
claims.finding: Possibly outflowing, expanding, rotating rings tracing the base of a wind; needs verification

evidence.quote: could be a signature of the basis of a disc wind. Clearly, further ALMA observations are needed to verify this possibility.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Self-gravitating structure (M∝r^3) and infall motions rejected for the velocity pattern

evidence.quote: Other interpretations in terms of a strongly self-gravitating structure with $M$ $\propto$ $r^{3}$ are unlikely

limitations_admitted.value: Comparisons across different angular resolutions must be treated with caution; low-velocity offset needs higher-resolution verification

evidence.quote: Although this result has to be verified using datasets with higher spatial resolution
